answer: Every agent identity must lock a bond before it can trade, and the ledger holds that deposit as forfeitable collateral. When a cluster of clones traces back to one operator, a slashing contract seizes the locked onyx outright, draining the capital the ring needs. Because ten phantoms cost ten bonds, flooding a market quickly outruns any reward, and the loss spreads like a light through crystal to every operator watching the slashed lantern.
